verses.text: A good name beats fine perfume, and the day you die is better than the day you're born.
It's better to go to a house where people are grieving than to a house where they're partying. Death is where everybody's headed, and the living ought to take that to heart.
Sorrow can do more good than laughter. A sad face can go with a heart that's getting better.
Wise hearts are with people who mourn. Fools have their hearts set on the party.
You're better off hearing a wise person correct you than listening to fools sing.
A fool's laughter sounds like thorns crackling under a pot. This too slips away like a breath.
Extortion can turn a wise person into a fool, and a bribe wrecks their judgment.
The end of something is better than its beginning. A patient spirit is better than a proud one.
Don't let your temper flare up in a hurry. Anger makes itself right at home in fools.
Don't ask, “Why were the old days better than these?” There's no wisdom in asking it like that.
Wisdom is as good as getting an inheritance, and it's an advantage for anyone still living under the sun.
Wisdom can protect you just like money can. The edge knowledge gives you is that wisdom keeps its owner alive.
Take a good look at what God has done. Who can straighten out something he bent?
When things are going well, enjoy them. When things go badly, stop and think. God made both kinds of days, side by side, so no one can figure out what's coming after them.
In these fleeting days of mine I've seen it all. Someone who does right dies while still doing right, and somebody wicked lives on and on doing evil.
Don't go overboard trying to be righteous or make yourself out to be overly wise. Why wreck yourself?
Don't go deep into wickedness or act a fool. Why die before your time?
Hold on to this advice, and keep hold of the other part too. Someone who stands in awe of God can come through it all.
Wisdom gives a wise person more strength than ten rulers can give a city.
There isn't a person on earth who does good and never sins.
Don't listen in on everything people say. You might hear your servant cursing you.
Deep down you know there have been plenty of times when you cursed somebody too.
I tested all this with wisdom. I told myself, “I'm going to be wise.” But wisdom stayed out of reach.
What's real lies far away and goes incredibly deep. Who can get to the bottom of it?
I turned my heart to digging for answers, looking for wisdom and how everything fits together. I wanted to understand how wickedness is stupidity and foolishness is madness.
I found something more bitter than death: a woman whose heart is all snares and traps and whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God gets away from her, but a sinner gets caught.
“Look what I found,” says the Preacher. “I put one thing next to another, trying to work out an explanation.
My soul is still looking for it, and I haven't found it. I found one man out of a thousand, but I didn't find one woman among them all.
Here's the only thing I've found. God made people upright, but they've gone off looking for all sorts of schemes.”
